grammar.title: Imperative Commands for Giving Directions
grammar.explanation:
When giving directions in Spanish, you use imperative (command) forms. The form depends on whether you are using tú (informal) or usted (formal):

• Tú commands (informal): Gira (turn), Sigue (continue), Cruza (cross)
• Usted commands (formal): Gire (turn), Siga (continue), Cruce (cross)

Common direction phrases:
• Gira/Gire a la izquierda/derecha - Turn left/right
• Sigue/Siga recto/derecho - Continue straight
• Cruza/Cruce la calle - Cross the street

The formal 'usted' form is more commonly used when asking strangers for directions.
